purpose: Authored multiple-choice assessments for Weeks 1-3 so the Foundations modules use deterministic, scenario-based Check scoring.
grading: Each question has one module-authored correctIndex. A week passes only when every authored question is answered correctly.

questions.prompt: Two designers use different layer conventions on one package. What is the strongest response?
options: Let each designer keep their preferred convention.
Agree a package standard, update the controlled template/standards and check affected sheets for consistency.
Move all geometry to one layer without checking the package standard.

questions.prompt: What should be confirmed before creating a reusable electrical drafting block?
options: Only the block's visual appearance.
Project standard, insertion behaviour, attributes and intended reuse across the package.
Whether the block can be copied into any future project without review.

questions.prompt: What demonstrates senior ownership before drafting starts?
options: Start drawing immediately and resolve missing information later.
Identify inputs, interfaces, assumptions and approval boundaries that could change the drawing.
Use the previous project as the design basis without checking its applicability.

questions.prompt: A template contains an outdated layer used by several existing sheets. What is the strongest senior response?
options: Delete the layer immediately because it is outdated.
Confirm the controlled standard, assess affected sheets, define the migration approach and verify the package after the change.
Leave the template unchanged forever to avoid coordination work.

questions.prompt: Why should drafting assumptions be recorded rather than kept as personal notes?
options: So another reviewer can see what was assumed, challenge it and confirm whether it affects design intent or approval.
So the drafter can avoid asking questions.
Because assumptions automatically become approved design decisions.

questions.prompt: A reference file changes after drafting has started. What should a senior designer consider first?
options: Reload it and accept every geometry change automatically.
Assess the reference revision/change, identify affected geometry and interfaces, then coordinate the impact before updating blindly.
Ignore the revision because references are outside the drawing.

questions.prompt: Why is a controlled MicroStation level structure important?
options: It makes every drawing use the same colours regardless of project requirements.
It makes graphics predictable, supports review/filtering and reduces coordination and editing errors.
It removes the need for references and model checks.

questions.prompt: What is stronger than checking only whether a MicroStation sheet looks correct?
options: Check model structure, references, attributes, annotation, standards and issue information as well as appearance.
Check only the title block and plot preview.
Check that the drawing opens without an error.

questions.prompt: A level name is technically valid but does not match the project's controlled naming convention. What should you do?
options: Keep it because the geometry is still visible.
Align it with the controlled convention and assess whether existing references, filters or sheets are affected.
Rename every level in the project without checking dependencies.

questions.prompt: A nested reference is displaying unexpected geometry. What is the strongest first step?
options: Delete the nested reference.
Trace the reference/nesting relationship and identify the source revision or display dependency before changing it.
Copy the visible geometry into the active model and detach everything.

questions.prompt: A redline changes equipment location but the upstream cable route may be affected. What is the strongest response?
options: Treat it as an isolated drafting edit.
Do not treat it as isolated; identify affected interfaces and verify electrical consequences before issue.
Apply the redline and leave coordination to construction.

questions.prompt: When should a drafter escalate rather than make an assumption?
options: Whenever a drawing contains a revision cloud.
When the change affects design intent, safety, compliance, interfaces or an approval boundary that has not been defined.
Only when another drafter asks for help.

questions.prompt: What makes a QA check senior-level?
options: It checks only linework, spelling and visual appearance.
It checks drawing correctness plus information, interfaces, revision status and design assumptions before issue.
It confirms that the file name is correct and then closes the review.

questions.prompt: A redline conflicts with the latest approved equipment schedule. What should happen before the redline is incorporated?
options: Use the redline because it is newer by definition.
Identify the conflict, confirm the controlled design input and resolve the discrepancy before issue.
Choose whichever option requires less drafting time.

questions.prompt: A drawing passes a visual check but its revision description does not match the actual change. What is the strongest response?
options: Issue it because the geometry is correct.
Correct the revision record and verify the change description, affected documents and issue status before release.
Remove the revision description so there is no inconsistency.
